title: Implement managed Nix build and activation contract
goal: Implement and review the fail-closed managed Nix/NixOS build and activation contract required by the canonical executor profile without performing runtime activation: bind repository/revision/control-release inputs, exact system-closure receipts, separate Build and Activation effect classes, receipt-bound activation inputs, rollback metadata and pre-effect denial semantics.

approval.note: This task is implementation-only. It may change and test repository code but may not activate, boot, restart or otherwise mutate a NixOS runtime. Real disposable activation and closure readback are delegated to successor task HEIM-PC-NIXOS-MIGRATION-V1-T004 after this implementation is terminal and reviewed.

acceptance.assertion: The implementation models Build and Activation as distinct effect classes: build-contract evaluation cannot change the active system, while activation requires a separately authorized receipt and runtime task.

The managed build contract binds repository, exact source revision, Control Release Set, Nix inputs, resource budgets, leases, effect class and bounded receipts; focused tests prove stale or incomplete bindings fail closed without live activation.

Receipt schemas and tests prove that a successful managed build result must expose and bind the exact immutable NixOS system closure, exact source revision and Control Release Set digest before it can become activation input.

Activation interfaces accept only a reviewed receipt bound to exact source revision, system closure, target and Activation effect class; caller-supplied closure strings, branch names or mutable source state alone are insufficient authority.

Next-boot and persistent activation interfaces are implemented to consume only the prebuilt approved closure and cannot silently reevaluate Git, branches, locks or remote inputs between review and activation.

Missing, stale, mismatched or unauthorized activation authority is rejected by the implementation before any runtime effect; effect-free tests prove the denied path cannot reach the activation executor.
Entrypoints and scripts remain adapters to the canonical managed-build/activation contract and cannot maintain a hidden second source of desired state, closure selection or activation authority.

Normal, boot-critical and destructive effects are classified by possible effect rather than filename or stated intent; ambiguous cases escalate fail-closed and destructive storage/firmware effects cannot use the normal rebuild path.

Activation receipt and executor contracts identify the prior/rollback closure and an explicit recovery path; effect-free tests prove rollback selection remains receipt-bound instead of reevaluating mutable source.

If a required activation or privilege primitive belongs to another canonical authority, the implementation uses that typed authority or creates an explicit dependency instead of duplicating a second truth or broad sudo/root shell path.

This task terminates without live NixOS activation, boot-state mutation, service restart, runtime rollback, production storage/EFI/Secure-Boot/firmware mutation, reboot or equivalent runtime effect; those proofs require successor task HEIM-PC-NIXOS-MIGRATION-V1-T004 or a later separately authorized cutover task.
Focused effect-free build/activation-contract/effect-classification tests plus required repository CI are green on the exact reviewed head before merge.
